Definition: from the pagan deity Ἀπόλλων (i.e. the sun; from G622); Apollonia, a place in Macedonia:--Apollonia.
BiblicalUsage: The name is a place on the road, nothing more. Paul and Silas passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia on their way to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews, in Acts 17:1 — Apollonia is one of the towns the gospel walked through without stopping.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the towns the apostles passed through matter too: the gospel was on foot, and every place it passed is part of the road it took.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
